explainer.heading: What happens
explainer.body: A comic-strip story. On a stormy midnight, Myla is reading “My Family and Other Animals” by Gerald Durrell with her friend Luke. They find themselves in the Durrells’ old house in Corfu and meet young Gerald, his mother Mrs Durrell and his animals. Gerald shows them around the island.

explainer.heading: The Durrell house
explainer.body: The house is old: the roof has holes, rain drips onto Gerald’s bed and there is no electricity — but it is big and has room for guests. Mrs Durrell says they moved from England, where it was cold and they were always ill; leaving was the best thing they ever did.
explainer.example: “Leaving was the best thing we ever did.” — Mrs Durrell

explainer.heading: Gerald and his animals
explainer.body: Gerald thinks swimming is boring and prefers exploring the island’s wildlife. He keeps bringing animals indoors (Mrs Durrell asks him to stop). Peli the pelican pushes Luke off a cliff while he looks at the view — Luke is safe. Gerald shows them his butterfly farm and shell collection; a butterfly lands on Myla’s nose. Myla gets the idea of an insect exhibition for the museum.

explainer.heading: About Gerald Durrell
explainer.body: Gerald Malcolm Durrell (born 1925 in Jamshedpur, India, to British parents) was a conservationist, zookeeper and writer. His first encounter with animals was at a zoo in India. He founded the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust and the Jersey Zoo. “My Family and Other Animals” was published in 1956.

explainer.heading: Vocabulary
explainer.body: Adjective suffix -al: nature → natural, environment → environmental, tradition → traditional, music → musical. Expressions with “take”: take place, take care of, take part in, take a break. House vs home: housework, homework, homesick, home-made, at home, household.

explainer.heading: Grammar: participles
explainer.body: A participle is a verb form used as an adjective or to build tenses. Present participle (-ing): an exciting book, a dripping roof. Past participle (-ed/-en): a broken roof, an excited girl. Participle phrases can join ideas: “Reading the book, Myla forgot the storm.”
explainer.example: exciting = causes the feeling; excited = has the feeling.

explainer.heading: Writing: a biography
explainer.body: A biography tells a real person’s life in the third person, in time order: birth and childhood, education, important events and achievements, later life, why they are remembered. Use past tense and dates.

questions.q: Write two facts about Gerald Durrell from the text.
questions.model: Gerald Durrell was born in Jamshedpur, India, in 1925 to British parents. He was a conservationist, zookeeper and writer who founded the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust and the Jersey Zoo. (Any two.)

questions.q: Describe Gerald as a boy from the story. What shows that he loves animals?
questions.model: Gerald is friendly and welcoming — he invites Myla and Luke to stay. He finds swimming boring and prefers exploring the island, which has lots of wildlife. He keeps bringing animals into the house, so his mother scolds him. He has a pet pelican, Peli, a butterfly farm and a shell collection. He dreams of having a real zoo one day. These show his deep love for animals.
points: Brings animals home; pelican, butterfly farm, shells
Dream of a zoo / love of animals concluded
